title: HIP RELIEF + MOBILITY
subtitle: LEFT HIP KINDNESS. SEATED THEN STANDING THEN FLOOR.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Today is a gentle left-hip and desk-fatigue session, about fourteen minutes. We stay seated first, then a short standing stretch, then we get down to the floor once at the end so you are not hopping up and down. Pain-free only. Skip anything that pinches the front of the hip. Smaller range is always fine.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall on a sturdy chair, feet flat, easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Same position if you can. No rush.
script.rest: Have a little rest. Breathe easy.
script.lastSet: Last set. Keep it comfortable and clean.
script.complete: That's us. Lovely work, Pam. Kind hips, easier desk fatigue, and another day in the book. Take your time getting up. See you tomorrow.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED KNEE LIFTS
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat and hip-width. Hands rest lightly on the sides of the seat or thighs. Soften the shoulders. Slowly lift one knee a few inches as if marching in place, then lower with control and switch sides. Alternate for eight lifts each side, or count eight total marches if that feels clearer. Breathe steadily. Keep the torso quiet — no leaning back or rocking. Feel a gentle wake-up through the front of the hips. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. A smaller lift is perfect.
exercises.speakStart: Seated knee lifts to warm the hips gently. Two sets of eight. Sit tall, feet flat, lift one knee a little, lower, then the other. Easy breath. Smaller is fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Feet flat. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Knee lifts done. Hips waking up kindly.

exercises.name: SEATED FIGURE FOUR
exercises.cue: Stay seated tall on the sturdy chair, feet flat. Cross the left ankle lightly over the right knee so the left shin is roughly horizontal — a gentle figure-four. Sit tall; do not yank the left knee down. Optional: hinge a tiny bit forward from the hips until you feel a mild stretch in the left outer hip or buttock. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds. If the front of the left hip pinches, stop and skip this one. Second set may repeat left, or lightly try the other side if it feels kind. Never force the knee. Sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness means stop.
exercises.speakStart: Seated figure four for the outer hip. Two sets of about twenty seconds. Left ankle lightly over the right knee. Sit tall. Do not force the knee down. If the front of the hip pinches, skip it.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Uncross gently. Easy breath.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside a sturdy chair. Place the right hand lightly on the chair back for support. Step the left foot back about half a step — not a deep lunge. Keep both feet pointing forward. Soften both knees. Gently tuck the pelvis under (think belt buckle toward the ribs) so you feel a mild stretch at the front of the left hip. Tiny lean of the torso forward is enough; do not sink into a big lunge. Breathe slowly for about twenty-five seconds. This is a small, kind stretch — not aggressive, not half-kneeling. Stop for sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. Use more chair support any time.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor stretch, left leg back. Three sets of about twenty-five seconds. Light hand on the chair, small step back, pelvis tucked, tiny lean. Not a deep lunge. Kind and small.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Step the feet together. Easy breath.

exercises.name: SUPINE BELLY BREATHING
exercises.cue: We get down to the floor once now and stay here for the rest. Lie on your back on a mat or carpet. Bend both knees, feet flat, about hip-width. Rest both hands on the belly. Soften the jaw and shoulders. Breathe in through the nose so the belly rises into your hands; breathe out slowly so the belly falls. No forcing, no breath-holding. About sixty seconds of calm belly breaths. If getting down was hard, take your time — we will finish on the floor so you only stand up once at the end. Stop if anything feels sharp or wrong.
exercises.speakStart: Down to the floor once for the rest of the session. Supine belly breathing, about sixty seconds. Knees bent, feet flat, hands on the belly. Soft in, soft out.
exercises.speakRest: Ten seconds. Stay comfortable on your back.

exercises.name: SUPINE HEEL SLIDES
exercises.cue: Stay on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Focus on the left leg. Slowly slide the left heel away along the floor so the left knee straightens a little, then slide it back in so the knee bends again. Smooth and slow — about eight reps. Keep the pelvis quiet and the back comfortable on the mat. Right foot can stay planted. Breathe out as you slide away if that helps. Only go as far as feels easy. Stop for sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. Smaller slide is always fine.
exercises.speakStart: Supine heel slides, left leg focus. Two sets of eight, slow. Slide the left heel away, then draw it back in. Quiet pelvis. Easy range.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Both knees bent. Easy breath.

exercises.name: SUPINE KNEE TO CHEST
exercises.cue: Stay on your back. Start with the right side: gently hug the right knee toward the chest with both hands, keeping the left knee bent or left foot flat. Soft hold about twenty seconds — not aggressive, not yanking. Then switch: gently hug the left knee toward the chest only if the left groin stays quiet. If the front of the left hip pinches or the groin complains, skip the left side and rest instead. Breathe slowly. Stop for sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Gentle knee to chest. Two sets of about twenty seconds each side. Right first, then left only if the left groin stays quiet. Soft hug, not aggressive. Skip if it pinches.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Both feet down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Knee to chest done. Kind work.

exercises.name: GLUTE BRIDGE
exercises.cue: Stay on your back, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width, arms relaxed by your sides. Press through the heels and lift the hips a modest amount so the body makes a gentle line from shoulders to knees — not a high arch. Squeeze the bottom lightly at the top, then lower slowly with control. Eight slow reps. Breathe out as you lift if that helps. Keep the ribs soft; do not fling the low back. Stop for sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. A smaller lift is perfect.
exercises.speakStart: Glute bridge, slow and modest. Two sets of eight. Feet flat, press through the heels, lift the hips a little, lower with control. Soft ribs.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty-five seconds. Hips down. Easy breath.

exercises.name: SIDE LYING CLAM
exercises.cue: Roll onto your right side so the left side is up (left is the top working leg). Knees bent about forty-five to ninety degrees, feet together, hips stacked. Head supported on your right arm or a small cushion. Keeping the feet touching, open the top (left) knee like a clam shell, then lower with control. Modest range only — no rolling the pelvis backward. Eight slow reps. Breathe steadily. Feel the outer left hip working gently. Stop for sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. After the last set, take your time to roll up to sitting, then stand using the chair.
exercises.speakStart: Side lying clam to finish, left side up. Two sets of eight. Hips stacked, feet together, open the top knee a little like a clam. Modest range. Then take your time getting up.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Knees together. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Clams done. That's the session. Take your time standing. Lovely work, Pam.
